apiDescriptions./ctp: CTP stands for Contoso Theme Parks, a fictional theme park company where a little wonder awaits every visitor. Discover Starlight Gardens and its Cloud Cruiser ride, check sample wait times, and explore a ride reservation from creation to cancellation. These static MockAPI examples do not store reservations or provide live availability; request bodies and query strings are ignored. Clearly labeled demo-faults routes demonstrate HTTP and connection failures.

endpoints.name: Discover the parks
endpoints.description: Welcome to Contoso Theme Parks! Discover the fictional Starlight Gardens park and its Cloud Cruiser attraction through a static 200 OK JSON response with an X-Mock-Source header. This endpoint supports GET only; use HEAD /ctp/health for the sample health check.

endpoints.name: Check the park API health
endpoints.description: Static HEAD-only health-check demo: always returns 200 OK with an X-Mock-Source header, no content type, and no body. No park services or dependencies are checked. GET on this path and HEAD /ctp/parks return 404. This is a mock endpoint subject to instance API-key protection, not MockAPI's public /health/live or /health/ready probes.

endpoints.name: Explore Cloud Cruiser
endpoints.description: Discover Cloud Cruiser in Starlight Gardens' Skyward Summit land. Returns static ride details with 200 OK, including its park ID, operating status, minimum height, and a link to sample wait times. No live ride, weather, or maintenance data is queried.

endpoints.name: Reserve a ride
endpoints.description: Make room for a little adventure! Simulates a Cloud Cruiser reservation for two visitors with 201 Created and Location: /ctp/reservations/42. The request body is ignored and every call returns the same sample reservation; nothing is stored or changed.

endpoints.name: View your ride reservation
endpoints.description: Returns sample reservation 42 for Cloud Cruiser with 200 OK. This is the destination of the creation response's Location header. The fixture is always available, even before creation or after cancellation; it is not a stored reservation.

endpoints.name: Check Cloud Cruiser wait times
endpoints.description: Check a sample 15-minute wait for Cloud Cruiser. Up to four requests in a rolling 10-second window return 200 OK; additional requests return 429 Too Many Requests with a themed JSON error and Retry-After: 10. The wait time is static, not live. The dashboard preselects five requests to demonstrate the limit, and both responses include repeated X-Mock-Source header values.

response.body: {"error":"wait_times_rate_limited","message":"Take a little breather! Check back in 10 seconds."}

endpoints.name: Cancel your ride reservation
endpoints.description: Plans change, and more adventures await. Simulates cancellation of reservation 42 with 204 No Content and an empty body. Nothing is deleted; repeated cancellations return the same response and GET /ctp/reservations/42 still returns the sample reservation.

endpoints.name: Find the featured attraction
endpoints.description: Follow today's spotlight to Cloud Cruiser. Returns 302 Found with Location: /ctp/attractions/cloud-cruiser and an empty body. Clients that follow redirects receive the ride's static 200 OK JSON details.

endpoints.name: Parade schedule fault demo
endpoints.description: Intentional HTTP failure demo: the fictional parade schedule service always returns 500 Internal Server Error with a themed JSON error. Use it to test client error handling; it does not cause a real application error or represent live park operations.

response.body: {"error":"parade_schedule_unavailable","message":"The parade schedule hit a little hiccup. Please try again later."}

endpoints.name: Ride sensor connection fault demo
endpoints.description: Intentional transport failure demo: the fictional Cloud Cruiser sensor connection is immediately aborted without an HTTP status, headers, or body. Test network-failure handling separately from HTTP errors. No real ride sensors or safety systems are involved.

endpoints.name: Reservation validation fault demo
endpoints.description: Intentional validation failure demo: always returns 422 Unprocessable Entity with application/problem+json and a sample partySize field error. Use it to test structured validation feedback. Request bodies are ignored, even when valid; no reservation is created and no actual validation is performed.

response.body: {"type":"about:blank","title":"Unprocessable Entity","status":422,"detail":"The sample reservation contains an invalid party size.","errors":{"partySize":["Party size must be between 1 and 6 visitors."]}}

endpoints.name: Reservation conflict fault demo
endpoints.description: Intentional business conflict demo: always returns 409 Conflict because the sample Cloud Cruiser ride slot is full. Use it to distinguish unavailable capacity from invalid input or a server failure. Request bodies are ignored; no live availability is checked and no reservation is stored.

response.body: {"type":"about:blank","title":"Conflict","status":409,"detail":"The sample Cloud Cruiser ride slot is full. Choose another time for your adventure.","attractionId":"cloud-cruiser"}

endpoints.name: Ticket service maintenance fault demo
endpoints.description: Intentional temporary unavailability demo: always returns 503 Service Unavailable with Retry-After: 30 and a static maintenance message. Use it to test maintenance messaging and retry handling separately from rate limiting. No real ticket service is contacted; waiting 30 seconds does not change the response.

response.body: {"type":"about:blank","title":"Service Unavailable","status":503,"detail":"The sample ticket service is taking a maintenance break. Please try again later."}

endpoints.name: Download the park schedule
endpoints.description: Take a little wonder with you! Returns a static Starlight Gardens schedule with 200 OK, text/csv, and Content-Disposition: attachment. Use it to test non-JSON responses and download headers. The sample times are fictional, not a live schedule; query strings do not select a different park or date.

response.body:
parkId,event,startTime
starlight-gardens,Park opening,09:00
starlight-gardens,Starlight parade,15:00
starlight-gardens,Park closing,21:00

endpoints.name: Update your ride reservation
endpoints.description: Bring more friends along! Simulates updating reservation 42 with 200 OK and a fixed party size of four. Request bodies are ignored and nothing is stored; GET /ctp/reservations/42 still returns the original two-visitor fixture. Includes fixed CORS headers for a non-credentialed cross-origin PATCH demo with the companion OPTIONS endpoint. Browser preflight requires instance API-key protection to be disabled.

endpoints.name: Check reservation preflight
endpoints.description: Explicit OPTIONS demo for reservation 42: returns 204 No Content, Allow: GET, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS, and fixed CORS headers permitting a non-credentialed PATCH with Content-Type and X-MockAPI-Key. Origin and requested method/header values are ignored; this is not dynamic CORS validation. Only the PATCH response includes matching CORS headers. Browser preflights do not carry the API key, so this cross-origin demo requires instance API-key protection to be disabled; this endpoint does not bypass protection.
